items.t: Shifter can reach Park while still in gear
items.job: Adjust or replace transmission shift cable
items.note: A shift cable recall covers affected cars. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Brake lights may stop working
items.note: Covered by a brake light switch recall for affected years. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Theta II engine bearing wear, knocking and seizure
items.note: Engine recalls and Kia's extended engine warranty often cover this. Keep oil-change records and check the VIN.

items.t: Fuel leak after an engine replacement
items.job: Dealer inspects and replaces the high-pressure fuel pipe if needed
items.note: Free under the fuel pipe recall for cars that had an engine replaced. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Airbags may not deploy in a crash
items.note: Free under the airbag control unit recall. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: ABS unit can short and catch fire
items.note: ABS recalls cover affected cars; the fix is often just a new fuse. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Right front axle shaft can crack and break
items.note: Free under the axle recall. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Driver airbag may not inflate fully
items.note: Free under the driver airbag recall. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Trunk cannot be opened from inside
items.job: Dealer replaces the trunk latch base
items.note: Free under recall 23V-594 (Kia SC278). Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Automatic emergency braking may not stop for parked cars
items.note: Free under the software recall. Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Fuel tank can swell, melt and leak
items.note: Free under the purge valve recall. If the fuel tank was damaged, replacing it costs much more.

items.t: Crankshaft sensor fault can stall the V6
items.note: Free under recall 03V-067. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Front subframe can rust through (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 09V-183. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Side airbag wiring can be damaged (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 01V-156. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Side curtain airbags may be installed wrong (K5 recall)
items.job: Inspect and refit side curtain airbags
items.note: Free under recall 23V-149. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Dual-clutch transmission can lose drive (K5 GT recall)
items.job: Replace dual-clutch transmission and update software
items.note: Free under recall 22V-760. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Steering can turn heavy with lane following on (K5 GT recall)
items.note: Free under recall 21V-447. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Rear window trim can come loose and fly off (K5 recall)
items.note: Free under recall 25V-493. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Parking lights can flicker (K5 recall)
items.note: Free under recall 25V-351. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Instrument display can go blank (K5 recall)
items.note: Free under recall 26V-046. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Fuel tank valve may not seal in a rollover (recall)
items.job: Dealer installs an additional fuel tank valve
items.note: Free under recall 04V-180. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Clock spring wiring can disable the driver airbag (recall)
items.job: Dealer replaces the clock spring contact assembly
items.note: Free under the clock spring recall (Kia SC094). Check the VIN first.

items.t: Low-pressure fuel hose can crack and leak (recall)
items.job: Dealer replaces the low-pressure fuel hose
items.note: Free under recall 20V-100. Check the VIN first.

items.t: Driver's door can stop unlatching
items.job: Replace door latch and lock actuator
items.note: Trim and door panel have to come off, so the labour is most of the bill.

items.t: Both low beam headlights can stop working
items.job: Replace low beam bulbs and inspect headlight wiring
items.note: A headlight assembly replacement costs far more than bulbs, so have the wiring checked first.

items.t: Engine can use up its oil between changes
items.job: Oil consumption test, then piston ring or short block repair
items.note: Check for extended engine coverage and the knock sensor software update before paying for the repair.

items.t: Headliner trim can come loose when side airbags fire
items.note: Free under recall 22V-560 (Kia SC245). Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Hybrid can lose power in electric mode
items.job: Dealer removes the voltage protection switch and fits redesigned battery management systems
items.note: Free under recall 18V-161 (Kia SC162). Check the VIN with a Kia dealer.

items.t: Airbag light from a failed passenger seat sensor mat
items.job: Dealer diagnoses and replaces the passenger seat sensor mat under Kia's warranty extension
items.note: Not a safety recall: Kia warranty extension WTY001/WTY002 covers the mat for 15 years with unlimited miles on all 2006-2010 Optimas. Owners without coverage report quotes of about $1,500.

items.t: Rough or hesitant shifts from the 8-speed automatic (2025)
items.note: Kia's warranty time in bulletin TSB 115 is 0.3 hours. Should be free under the new-car warranty.

items.t: Check engine light with code P2B59 (coolant flow valve)
items.note: The bulletin lists 0.3 hours. Should be free under the new-car warranty.

items.t: Low oil level warning even when the oil is full (2026)
items.note: Kia's warranty time in bulletin 265 is 0.4 hours. Free under the new-car warranty, and may come over the air.

items.t: Timing belt can snap and wreck the engine
items.job: Replace timing belt, tensioner and idler pulleys
items.note: Low parts figure is a Gates T313 belt for the 2.4L ($49 at FinditParts); genuine Kia belts are about $82 (2.4L) to $145 (V6) at KiaPartsNow, and KBB lists $484–$534 in dealer parts with the tensioner and idlers. Hours follow KBB dealer labor of $726–$802 for a 2005 Optima. YourMechanic estimates $1,061–$1,215 for 2001–2006 models. If the belt has already broken, bent valves make the repair far more expensive.

items.t: Throttle position sensor fault causes rough idle and stalling
items.note: No parts-retailer price was found, so this is based on YourMechanic: about $97 parts and $95 labor ($192 total). RepairPal: $163–$192 total for a 2004 Optima. The engine computer update in Kia bulletins may add time.

items.t: Hard downshift or jerk when slowing to a stop
items.job: Transmission fluid change, computer update and shift relearn
items.note: KBB 2008 Optima transmission fluid change: $128–$151 parts and $157–$185 labor at a dealer ($264–$309 total at an independent shop). Kia bulletin 1067 (2009–2010 2.4L) adds an engine computer update, a reset of the learned shift values and a relearn drive; no time was published for that, so it may add to the bill. A rebuild or replacement transmission costs far more.

items.t: Shudder or jerky launches from the dual-clutch transmission (K5 GT)
items.job: Replace dual clutch assembly after Kia judder test
items.note: Kia bulletin TRA100 lists 0.3 hours for the judder test and 4.5 hours to replace the dual clutch assembly (part 41000-2N510) on the K5. Part prices: $783 (OEMHyundaiParts, shared with Hyundai) to $952 (KiaPartsNow), MSRP $1,404. Software updates SA502/SA526 are separate and usually free. Should be covered by Kia's powertrain warranty for original owners.

items.t: Tire sidewall bulges or blowouts on newer K5s
items.note: SimpleTire lists 235/45R18 tires (the EX and GT-Line size) from about $81 to $292 each. Mounting and balancing are extra and are usually a flat shop fee. Ask the tire maker about a warranty claim first.
